subject.title: Gateway memory growth due to repeated file read errors

question: Should this issue be fixed by changing the generic `read` tool behavior for directories/missing workspace memory paths, or by finding and correcting the scheduler/prompt producer that requests `memory-system/CORE.md` and `memory/agent-tasks`?
rationale: Current source already has partial mitigations, but the unresolved symptoms cross tool semantics and scheduler/agent prompt ownership; choosing the generic behavior could alter all read-tool callers.

options.title: Live repro first
options.body: Keep this open for a maintainer or validation agent to capture a current Gateway run showing the exact scheduled turn, tool-call args, and RSS trend before selecting a fix boundary.

options.title: Generic read semantics
options.body: Define `read` on directories and selected missing daily-memory paths as non-error context, then add focused read-tool tests and a compatibility note for all agent callers.

options.title: Producer-only repair
options.body: Treat `read` as file-only and fix whichever scheduler/prompt path is generating stale CORE.md and agent-tasks reads once the live producer is identified.

recommendation.title: Live repro first
recommendation.body: Keep this open for a maintainer or validation agent to capture a current Gateway run showing the exact scheduled turn, tool-call args, and RSS trend before selecting a fix boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The current read-tool behavior and daily-memory mitigation are in the area most directly implicated by the remaining product-boundary choice.
